title: A five-minute energy walk-through
description: One slow walk around your home with fresh eyes can spot the leaks, lights and leftovers that quietly waste energy.

body.heading: Walk it like a visitor
paragraphs: Start at the front door and walk through your home as if you were seeing it for the first time. Look for lights left on in empty rooms, chargers plugged in with nothing attached, and heating warming spaces nobody is in.
Take a phone or a notebook and simply list what you find. The point of the walk is noticing, not fixing everything on the spot. A list turns vague guilt into a handful of specific, doable jobs.

body.heading: Feel for the invisible
paragraphs: Run the back of your hand around window frames, the letterbox and the loft hatch. Moving air on a cool day reveals draughts your eyes would miss, and most small gaps can be sealed cheaply.

Check the hot water cylinder or tank if you have one: a jacket or insulation on exposed pipes keeps heat where you want it. Note radiators hidden behind long curtains or furniture, which warm the wall more than the room.

body.heading: Pick three, not thirty
paragraphs: From your list, choose the three easiest wins: perhaps a draught strip, a timer on a heater, and switching the busiest bulbs to LED. Small, finished changes build the confidence to tackle bigger ones later.
Repeat the walk each season. Heating habits matter most in winter, shading and ventilation in summer, and a fresh walk catches the things that changed since last time.

takeaway: Walk through slowly, write down what you notice, and fix the three easiest things first.
